H1-1: How to Choose Trail Running Shoes
Copy 1: Choosing trail running shoes comes down to fit, terrain and how far you run. Start with the surface: road running needs cushioning and a smooth sole, while trails need grip and protection. Then think about distance, because comfort matters more the longer you are out. Deeper lugs suit mud, and a rock plate helps on stony ground. Try several pairs, run in them if you can, and replace them when the cushioning feels flat or the tread has worn.
